answer_text:
Here's a comprehensive guide to the **best websites for free 3D game assets** in 2026:

---

## 🎮 Top Free 3D Game Asset Sources

### 1. 🏆 [Kenney.nl](https://kenney.nl)
This one-person operation has released over 40,000 assets — all CC0, all free, no sign-up required. The art style is clean, colourful, and remarkably consistent across packs, which means you can mix and match assets without your game looking inconsistent. The site offers 2D assets, 3D models, UI elements, fonts, and audio.
- **License:** CC0 (Public Domain) — no attribution needed
- **Best for:** Rapid prototyping, stylized games, UI elements

---

### 2. 🌿 [Quaternius](https://quaternius.com)
If you're making a 3D game with a stylised low-poly look, Quaternius is essential. This artist has released thousands of models — characters, animals, vehicles, environments, weapons — all under CC0. The signature "Quaternius style" is instantly recognisable: clean geometry, bright colours, charming animations. Assets come rigged and animated, ready to drop into Unity, Unreal, or Godot.
- **License:** CC0
- **Best for:** Low-poly 3D games, animated characters

---

### 3. 🌄 [Poly Haven](https://polyhaven.com)
Poly Haven started as HDRI Haven and has grown into a comprehensive library of 3D models, HDRIs, and textures — all CC0. The models tend toward realistic props and environmental pieces rather than stylised game assets, but they're high quality and instantly usable. No sign-up required. Just download what you need.
- **License:** CC0
- **Best for:** Realistic 3D assets, environment art, lighting/HDRIs

---

### 4. 🖼️ [Sketchfab](https://sketchfab.com)
Sketchfab is a huge repository of 3D models, and while many are for sale, there's a substantial number of models available for free. The platform's built-in 3D viewer is a great feature, allowing you to inspect every angle of a model before you download it. Just be sure to check the licensing for each model, as they can vary.
- **License:** Varies (CC0 / CC BY)
- **Best for:** Wide variety of models across all categories

---

### 5. 🎭 [itch.io](https://itch.io/game-assets/free/tag-3d)
Itch.io is a popular platform for indie game developers to host and sell their games, but it also has a massive section for game assets. You can find a wide variety of free 3D game assets, from character models to environmental packs, often with very permissive licenses. The community-driven nature of Itch.io means you'll discover unique and creative assets you won't find anywhere else.
- **Best for:** Unique, creative community assets

---

### 6. 🎨 [Mixamo](https://www.mixamo.com) *(Adobe)*
Mixamo offers 2,000+ free animations with auto-rigging, making it one of the best sources for character animations and rigged 3D characters. Great for humanoid models.
- **Best for:** Character animations, auto-rigging

---

### 7. 🏪 [Unity Asset Store (Free Section)](https://assetstore.unity.com/top-assets/top-free)
The Unity Asset Store (Free section) hosts 10,000+ Unity-optimized assets. 3D is Unity's bread and butter with 41k assets available, and you'll find plenty of low poly meshes as well as a few pre-made animations.
- **Best for:** Unity developers looking for engine-ready assets

---

### 8. 🔲 [OpenGameArt](https://opengameart.org)
OpenGameArt has been around for over a decade and hosts a massive collection of 2D art, 3D models, music, and sound effects — all under open licences like CC0, CC-BY, or GPL.
- **Best for:** Large variety, open-source projects

---

### 9. 📸 [Quixel Megascans / Fab](https://quixel.com)
Quixel is releasing a final, offline version of Quixel Mixer, along with the option to download over 800 free Quixel Megascans assets. It's a pioneer in the creation of photogrammetry-based 3D assets, delivering photorealistic models compatible with any engine. All assets are scanned from real-world objects using purpose-built hardware.
- **Best for:** AAA-quality photorealistic assets, Unreal Engine projects

---

### 10. 🆓 [Free3D](https://free3d.com)
A large number of the recent models have a lower polygon count and can be used in games straight away, covering categories like houses, buildings, medieval, fantasy, cities, and more. Free3D also hosts several low poly models made specifically for real-time usage.
- **Best for:** Vehicles, architecture, props, weapons

---

## 📋 Quick Tips

- Safe commercial licenses include CC0 (Public Domain) — unrestricted use, no attribution required — CC BY (Attribution) — free with credit to creator — and MIT License, a permissive open-source license.
- GLB and glTF are the recommended formats because all textures, materials, and animations are bundled in one file, with native support in Three.js, Babylon.js, Unity, and Unreal.
- Consider using a complete asset pack to develop your game if possible. Asset packs often include everything you need to create a game world and are a fantastic way to keep your game art looking consistent.
